summary: Ethereum is a decentralized blockchain with smart contract functionality, launched in 2015 by Vitalik Buterin and others. It is the second-largest cryptocurrency by market capitalization and transitioned from proof-of-work to proof-of-stake in 2022, cutting energy usage by over 99%. The platform supports decentralized applications, DeFi, and NFTs, and has undergone multiple upgrades including Dencun and Pectra.

claims.text: Ethereum is a decentralized blockchain with smart contract functionality.
claims.evidence_quote: Ethereum is a decentralized blockchain with smart contract functionality.

claims.text: Ether is second only to bitcoin in market capitalization among cryptocurrencies.
claims.evidence_quote: Among cryptocurrencies, ether is second only to bitcoin in market capitalization.

claims.text: Ethereum was conceived in 2013 by programmer Vitalik Buterin.
claims.evidence_quote: Ethereum was conceived in 2013 by programmer Vitalik Buterin.

claims.text: The network went live on 30 July 2015.
claims.evidence_quote: the network went live on 30 July 2015.

claims.text: On 15 September 2022, Ethereum transitioned from proof-of-work to proof-of-stake in an update known as 'The Merge', which cut the blockchain's energy usage by over 99%.
claims.evidence_quote: On 15 September 2022, Ethereum transitioned its consensus mechanism from proof-of-work (PoW) to proof-of-stake (PoS) in an update known as "The Merge", which cut the blockchain's energy usage by over 99%.

claims.text: In 2016, The DAO raised a record US$150 million in a crowd sale.
claims.evidence_quote: raised a record US$150 million in a crowd sale

claims.text: The DAO was exploited in June 2016 when US$50 million of DAO tokens were stolen by an unknown hacker.
claims.evidence_quote: US$50 million of DAO tokens were stolen by an unknown hacker.

claims.text: The DAO hack led to a hard fork that split Ethereum into two blockchains: Ethereum and Ethereum Classic.
claims.evidence_quote: The fork resulted in the network splitting into two blockchains: Ethereum with the theft reversed, and Ethereum Classic which continued on the original chain.

claims.text: In March 2017, the Enterprise Ethereum Alliance was announced with 30 founding members.
claims.evidence_quote: In March 2017, various blockchain startups, research groups, and Fortune 500 companies announced the creation of the Enterprise Ethereum Alliance (EEA) with 30 founding members.

claims.text: In January 2018, the ERC-721 Non-Fungible Token Standard was published, introducing the first official NFT standard on Ethereum.
claims.evidence_quote: In January 2018, a community-driven paper (an EIP, "Ethereum Improvement Proposal") under the leadership of civic hacker and lead author William Entriken was published, called ERC-721: Non-Fungible Token Standard.

claims.text: In March 2021, Visa announced that it began settling stablecoin transactions using Ethereum.
claims.evidence_quote: In March 2021, Visa Inc. announced that it began settling stablecoin transactions using Ethereum.

claims.text: In April 2021, JP Morgan Chase, UBS, and MasterCard invested US$65 million into ConsenSys.
claims.evidence_quote: JP Morgan Chase, UBS, and MasterCard announced that they were investing US$65 million into ConsenSys

claims.text: The London upgrade in August 2021 included EIP-1559, which burns a portion of transaction fees, potentially reducing ether's inflation rate.
claims.evidence_quote: The London upgrade included Ethereum Improvement Proposal ("EIP") 1559, a mechanism for reducing transaction fee volatility. The mechanism causes a portion of the ether paid in transaction fees for each block to be destroyed rather than given to the block proposer, reducing the inflation rate of ether and potentially resulting in periods of deflation.

claims.text: The Dencun upgrade on 13 March 2024 introduced 'blobs' for cheaper data availability, reducing costs for Layer 2 networks.
claims.evidence_quote: On 13 March 2024, "Dencun" or also "Deneb-Cancun" set of upgrades went live. These included EIP-4844 (Proto-Danksharding) which introduced "blobs" that can be used for general-purpose data-availability.

claims.text: The Pectra update was launched on 7 May 2025.
claims.evidence_quote: The Prague-Electra ("Pectra") update was launched on 7 May 2025.
